pointers.sentence: A migration file is a module that defines one class, named `Migration`, a subclass of the class of that name in `django.db.migrations` (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration`).
When Django loads the file it makes one instance of the class, giving it the module's name and the application's label (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.load_disk`).

Each entry of `operations` is an **operation**, an instance of a subclass of `Operation` (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation`): here two of `CreateModel`, each holding a model's name and its fields.
Django's description of the models is the **project state**, a `ProjectState` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState`).

For them a project state is **rendered**: each model state is made into a model class, a **historical model**, and registered in a registry that belongs to the state, **the state's registry**, apart from the main registry in which the models of the project live (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.apps`, `django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.render`).

For them a project state is **rendered**: each model state is made into a model class, a **historical model**, and registered in a registry that belongs to the state, **the state's registry**, apart from the main registry in which the models of the project live (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.apps`, `django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.render`).
The check that follows it is a separate matter, that the history recorded in the database is not out of order (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.handle`).
The **autodetector** is given the two and finds operations that turn the first into the second (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes`).
The **writer** turns each migration into the text of a module, once for each file; the quote stops at the first (`django/db/migrations/writer.py:MigrationWriter.as_string`).
The five migrations and their dependencies make the graph, in which an edge runs from a node to each of its **parents**, the migrations it depends on (`django/db/migrations/graph.py:MigrationGraph`).
The **executor**, a `MigrationExecutor`, is made for one connection, and it makes a loader with that connection (`django/db/migrations/executor.py:MigrationExecutor`).
A clone of that state goes to `MigrationExecutor.migrate`, which has the recorder make its table and then carries out the plan (`django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).
For each migration the executor opens a schema editor, and `Migration.apply` goes through the operations in order (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`).
A migration is **applied** on a database when the table there has its row, and beside its id a row holds a label, a name and a time, no more (`django/db/migrations/recorder.py:MigrationRecorder`).
